notes.body:
- **Ten reworked pre-cons replace their old versions**, chosen by a computer-vs-computer test (each version played every other deck once; 2,006 of 2,496 games; the version with the better win rate won, a tie kept the old): Ardnia's Abundance, Auviin's Abeyant, Evora's Excellence, Leonhart's Lions, Mordrec's Malice, Persea's Pessimism, Romuden's Roost, Snaebjörn's Snacks, Verren's Verdict, and Roldage's Ragtag, now **Roldage's Raiders**. Each old version is kept as a saved deck, "<name> (previous)", for a longer test later; the 14 reworks that lost stay as their saved decks.
- The computer's AI-Stress decks are gone: the computer plays the pre-cons.

- **Deck Builder:** the scroll wheel turns the page over the card grid. Searching "mill" also finds cards that put cards from a deck into a graveyard without saying "mill".
- **Plasma Field** stays where it is until it has been activated; after it moves it is face down and asleep again.
- **Forbidden Resonator** shows the card discarded for it, and that discard now sets off discard triggers.
- **Storm-Rigger** is a Resonance (its Shock goes on the Stack). **Grounding Chain** also deactivates. **Coral Trident** gives the Dominate to the equipped Summon in its text. **Prepared Protector** has 1 Attack. **Minotaur Gorer** lim 4.
- Larger text on Churn, Qadir's Gabl, Soulsnatcher Lich's Manifest and Ifrit's Lamp.

- **The Lightning batch, part two: six new cards**, and Lightning's slots are full. Ring for the Talentless and Ionomancer (Rares); Unmitigated Anger, Borrowed Lightning, Plasma Field and Disrupted Vectors (Special Rares).
- **A card can make you lose:** Borrowed Lightning's [2][2 Lightning] is paid at the next End Phase, or its caster loses the game.
- Ring for the Talentless hands on the entering Summon's keywords; its other abilities aren't lent yet.

- **The Lightning batch, part one: sixteen new cards.** Restless Coilhand, Trapwarden Golem, Charged Up, Stormeye Naga, Galvanic Baton, Live Ground, Fulgurite Strike, Nerve Jolt and Rakshasa Tithe-Taker (Commons); Lost in Chaos, Reversed Polarity, Quatl Pathfinder, Thunderclap, Afterimage, Arc Reversal and Raining Bolts (Uncommons). The Rares and Special Rares follow.
- **Shocking Ground**, Lightning's hazard: a Summon that enters it is Shocked until its controller's next Active Phase. It lasts 3 rounds.
- **Rakshasa** is a new tribe.
- Pyromaniac and Cryomancer reworded ("Perpetual - Spells you control that ..."), same effect; Whisperwing Adept is a Wizard.
- Meek Counters show on the board with the designer's new icon.
- The computer sacrifices to Soul-Hungry Locket more carefully: tokens, Summons that can't act, and cheap Demise cards - never a strong working Summon.

- **The attacker picks the protector for a Spell too.** When you cast a Spell that deals damage or life loss at a Guardian with two or more Guardprotect protectors, you are asked which of them takes it, the same way a Shockwave asks at the attack. Hits that aren't aimed (drains, Demise, Traps, Curses) still go to the protector closest to death.

Four rulings the game did not follow yet:
- **A Summon pushed, pulled or swapped onto your Step Trap sets it off** (the forced-movement ruling). Sliding over one still does not, and Gallows Step and the other "moves onto" Traps still want the Summon's own move.
- **Mordrec's Gabl is a true replacement:** a Summon he sends into the Void instead of the graveyard fires no Demise. He asks at the death, before anything resolves.
- **Crystal Bastion is one of the protectors you pick from:** a Shockwave asks which protector takes it (Bastion or Summon) on a Summon or a Building. With no pick, the one nearest death takes it.
- **Goad adds up:** a printed Goad plus Bountyleaf Ranger's granted Goad is +2. Before, the printed one hid the grant. Two Rangers give Goad 2.
- **The rules codex** now carries the five forced-movement rulings of 2026-09-29 (rules-core.md, Movement).

The designer's rulings on the website's open points:
- **A kill resolves inside combat, Onslaught after it.** When one attack kills, its Dominate and the victim's Demise now resolve before the attacker's Onslaught.
- **Elusive answers any ability that targets its Summon** - an enemy Manifest, Infiltrate or Agility included, not only Spells and activated abilities.
- **Nothing is immune to Poison:** the last of the old Mechanical exception is gone from Venomous and Contagious.
- **In-game reminders corrected:** Chill ("deactivates and depletes; a target already deactivated becomes Frozen"), Devotion (a taunt - "enemies can't attack your other Summons in its zone"; it absorbs nothing), Shadow Step and Shadow Cloak ("if active").
- **The rules codex** records those rulings, Petrified as an ordinary ailment that a cleanse removes, and ten stale passages fixed (Fogged against Guardians, Stealth against attacks, Leaping, Deep Infiltration, Seabound, the Avert count, spelling).

- **Wild Blessing and Safe Scouting can be cast again.** Neither accepted any target - not even yours - since they were added; a new test sweeps every targeted Spell for that gap.
- **The computer no longer stops playing when it has a Trap set.** The Energy it keeps back to spring the Trap was added to every price, a free Worker's included, so it could sit for turns with cards in hand; a free play is never held back now.
- **The computer listens to its own "no" for 32 Spells.** Their rules said not to cast them (The Final Dawn on a full board of its own, Forestry with no Nature Worker in the deck, Northern Lore from a deck of five...), and a general rule cast them anyway.
- **The computer casts Savage Pounce and Anticipation** (it planned them and never said X, so the cast was refused), Anticipation on the Summons its plan chose, and **Quick Reflexes** only when there is a discarded Lightning card to return.
